name: Good Neighbors: Life Inside the Helix Family
description: A warmly produced lifestyle drama following three HelixCorp employee families living in a Tier 4 residential node, navigating promotions, relationship milestones, and the cheerful minor frictions of managed community living. Every conflict resolves through proper corporate HR channels; every hardship is met with a HelixCorp wellness benefit. The show ran for fourteen seasons before being quietly archived when ratings analytics revealed it was being watched ironically by Tier 2 audiences at scale.
cultural_impact: Good Neighbors became the definitive template for corporate propaganda drama — studied by independent media critics as a masterclass in aspirational class-washing.
story_hooks: A Tier 2 mesh archivist has collected every scrubbed frame from the show and believes the background props form a pattern — a deliberate leak from someone inside HelixCorp's production office.
A cast member defects from the show's promotional circuit and tries to reach underground journalists with information about what the production staff were contractually forbidden to say.
A player character is hired to track down the ironic viewing collective responsible for the viral re-edit that got the show archived — HelixCorp wants names.
